external_public_type_dependencies.name: GtkWidget
external_public_type_dependencies.header_strategy: Forward-declared by ghostty/gtk.h rather than including the GTK header.
external_public_type_dependencies.implication: The ABI is language-neutral C but not GTK-neutral: consumers must bind GTK's GObject/widget type and ownership/lifetime rules. The public transfer ambiguity on the constructor remains a blocker for a safe Rust wrapper.

prerequisites.requirement: The successful runtime constructor must be called on the GTK main thread before gtk_init() and before constructing any GTK object.
prerequisites.current_positive_evidence: crates/zentty-linux/src/main.rs and linux/tests/api-contract.c construct the runtime before gtk_init in their successful paths.
prerequisites.missing_misuse_evidence: No fresh-process negative test calls gtk_init or constructs a GTK object first and then proves that both runtime constructors fail safely with an actionable diagnostic.
prerequisites.recommendation: Keep this as an explicit safe-adapter construction precondition and add the proposed ghostty-runtime-initialization-order contract cell before product integration.

abi_defects.finding: ghostty_gtk_embed_async_backend_t is a public C enum whose size and compatible integer type are implementation-defined, while ghostty_gtk_embed_runtime_new_with_async_backend accepts c_int in Zig. A consumer built with -fshort-enums can use a one-byte enum even though the Zig boundary declares an int-sized value.
abi_defects.impact: The three numeric values and current C/C++ syntax assertions do not prove layout or calling-convention compatibility. C, C++, generated Rust bindings, or another target/compiler configuration can disagree at the unsafe ABI boundary.
abi_defects.current_evidence_limit: api-header-cpp.cc proves only that the type is an enum and that values are 0/1/2; it does not assert sizeof, alignment, compatible integer type, or Rust FFI representation, and build-local does not compile the consumer with -fshort-enums.
abi_defects.local_observation: At this checkpoint, linux/tests/ghostty-async-backend-abi reported sizeof=4 with default compiler flags and sizeof=1 with -fshort-enums in both C17 and C++17, then exited 99 as the tracked XFAIL requires. This deterministic header-representation evidence does not call the real library or exercise Rust.
abi_defects.required_proof: Use an explicitly fixed-width public ABI representation or otherwise guarantee the declared representation, then test C17 and C++17 with default flags and -fshort-enums plus the raw Rust binding's size/alignment/call behavior against the real library.
abi_defects.recommendation: Do not ratify or safely bind this constructor signature until the representation defect is repaired and the cross-language contract cell passes.

version_policy_gaps: The version script assigns all twelve exports to GHOSTTY_GTK_EMBED_1.0, but linux/tests/abi-surface strips @version suffixes and therefore does not verify the node.
There is no compile-time ABI macro or runtime version/query symbol, so an old/new mismatch cannot be rejected before unsafe calls.
No symbol-node evolution or deprecation policy is documented.
The header and version script are Linux/ELF-oriented; visibility/version behavior on other GTK targets is unqualified.
